title: The Old Lighthouse
text:
In the short story, an elderly keeper lives alone on a small island. Every evening he climbs the stairs of the lighthouse to light the lamp, even though no ships have passed for years. His daughter writes letters asking him to move to the city. He never answers them, because he believes that someone will eventually need the light.

One stormy night, a small boat appears near the rocks. The keeper keeps the lamp burning all night and guides the boat safely into the harbour. The next morning, the young sailor thanks him and asks why he never gave up. The keeper simply smiles and says that the light was never only for the ships.

questions.text: Why does the keeper climb the lighthouse every evening?
options: To count the boats that pass by
To send letters to his daughter
To light the lamp although no ships pass

questions.text: What does the young sailor do the next morning?
options: He leaves the island at dawn
He asks the keeper why he never gave up
He writes a letter to the keeper's daughter

questions.text: What can be inferred about the keeper's attitude toward his work?
options: He is bored and wants to leave the island
He is loyal to a purpose that gives his life meaning
He is afraid of the sea
He works only because he is paid

questions.text: What is the main message of the keeper's final words?
options: Lights should be kept only for ships
A purpose can matter even when nobody seems to see it
Sailors should always thank their guides
The sea is too dangerous to cross

vocabulary.definition: a tall tower with a powerful light that warns and guides ships
after a long time or after a process has happened
a sheltered area of water where boats can stop safely
leads or directs someone along a safe way

paragraph_translations: En el relato, un guardián anciano vive solo en una pequeña isla. Cada tarde sube las escaleras del faro para encender la lámpara, aunque no han pasado barcos durante años. Su hija le escribe cartas pidiéndole que se mude a la ciudad. Él nunca responde, porque cree que algún día alguien necesitará la luz.

Una noche de tormenta, un pequeño bote aparece cerca de las rocas. El guardián mantiene la lámpara encendida toda la noche y guía al bote con seguridad hasta el puerto. A la mañana siguiente, el joven marinero le agradece y le pregunta por qué nunca se rindió. El guardián sonríe y responde que la luz nunca fue solo para los barcos.
